messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Post-hoc thinning
parts:
Is there a quick way to thin the output of rstan::stan() after-the-fact? I can see that one could subset each entry in the samples attribute of the rstan::stan() output, but there seem to be numerous other references to the number of iterations, warm-up, etc that should be modified before one can use ggmcmc. Just wondering if anyone has already written code for this so I don't re-invent the wheel.

Mike
